title: CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF THE CENTRAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTER
full_text:
CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF THE CENTRAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTER
Annex 1 to the Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases <Newly inserted on June 22, 2023>
(Relating to Article 6 (1))

1. General criteria
(a) The center shall have the clinical and research capabilities necessary to play a leading role in national cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(b) The center shall have the facilities, equipment, and personnel necessary to provide education and training for persons engaged in cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(c) The center shall have personnel capable of evaluating regional and local cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers.
(d) The center shall have specialist personnel and equipment for registration projects, surveys, and research relating to cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(e) The center shall have specialist personnel and equipment capable of supporting national statistical data and policy projects concerning cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

2. Organizational operation criteria
(a) A director and a deputy director of the central cardio-cerebrovascular disease center shall be appointed to perform the duties under Article 12 (1) of the Act.
(b) The director shall be appointed, in consultation with the Minister of Health and Welfare, from among medical personnel under the Medical Service Act who have at least ten years of experience in clinical practice, research, or policy support in the field of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
(c) The director's term shall be at least two years, and professional expertise and independence in the performance of duties shall be guaranteed.
(d) The central center shall be organized and operated independently, separately from other organizational structures.
(e) Separate teams shall be established and operated for building a nationwide cooperative system for cardio-cerebrovascular disease management; supporting the operation and evaluation of regional and local centers; conducting research on cardio-cerebrovascular diseases; and providing preventive education and publicity concerning cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
